newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end up sharply on cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end up sharply on cash ideas.

text.p: Talk of increased cash business boosted CME lumber futures up into technical buy orders and prices ended sharply higher, traders said.
Lumber closed $7.90 to $0.50 per tbf higher with May up most at $398.40 and July up $5.50 at $398.70 per tbf.
The market had shown technical support early, after holding the $388 level in both May and July Monday, and moved up into buy stops as talk of increased cash business added to demand, traders said.
"There is a little better tone to the cash market," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
"It sounds like a lot of cheap wood, at least, is starting to disappear. It's a better tone, not better prices in the cash market," Schmaedick said.
The $400 level provided some resistance to futures and the market will have to cash higher before going through this area, traders added.
